BLOCKER: FR-3 (AC-3) is self-contradictory: preconditions say "DB mode on", acceptance says "Given DB on ... Then it fails closed", and the FR-3 title/triggers repeat on-mode guard behavior — the approved AC-3 (off mode keeps file authority) is not actually specified or testable as written.

No distinct evidence/tests exist for AC-4's operator-recovery runbook path; all four ACs point to one pytest command that cannot demonstrate runbook coverage (stop condition "Missing tests for read/write/delete/ID" is unproven).
MAJOR: `PF_BACKLOG_DB` valid values include `dual` and `shadow`, but the operation_matrix/failure_matrix only define `on` and `off` behavior for unlisted scopes — unlisted-scope semantics under dual/shadow are unspecified, risking a silent file fallback through an undefined mode.
Design does not address CL-011: no runtime role posture (NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS) or tenant-binding proof for the guard, despite `security_threat_model` and `rls_tenant` being marked APPLICABLE.

Design guardrail checklist items 2 (availability/SPOF: worker/DB down behavior, on-startup check), 4 (blast radius/dry-run), 5 (id/sequence invariants for ID-allocation path) are unanswered in the design pack.
MINOR: Rollback is inconsistent: item says "Revert the change", design says "Set PF_BACKLOG_DB=off explicitly" — two different rollback procedures with no precedence stated.
Config contract `startup_validation` for `PF_BACKLOG_DB` is "operation" (lazy) rather than on-startup, weakening CL-014-style defence-in-depth; failure surfaces only at first use.
Observability is limited to "error code logged with scope" — no metric/counter for `BACKLOG_DB_SCOPE_UNLISTED` occurrences, so fail-closed spikes are not alertable.
`affected_files`/`in_scope` contain "Not specified." placeholders; CL-016 separation of prerequisites (BI-PF-1531) from changed files is not explicit in scope.
Off-mode operation_matrix covers only read/write for unlisted scopes; delete/ID off-mode behavior is unlisted despite AC-2/AC-4 covering those paths.
NIT: Error taxonomy defines only `BACKLOG_DB_SCOPE_UNLISTED`; consider whether mode/allowlist misconfiguration (`BACKLOG_DB_MODE_INVALID`) needs an equivalent documented recovery step in the runbook.
`ac_evidence.sha` values are "candidate" rather than pinned SHAs; traceability is weaker than a content-addressed evidence reference.
SUMMARY: Direction is right (fail closed, no silent fallback, explicit off), but AC-3 is specified inconsistently within FR-3 itself and AC-4's runbook/test evidence is not concretely demonstrated — these must be fixed before Gate 1.5.
Undefined dual/shadow semantics for unlisted scopes is the top residual risk of reintroducing the silent file fallback this item exists to remove.

Guardrail gaps (RLS/role posture, startup validation, availability/invariants) and a dual rollback definition need design answers; no schema/API/language-rule violations found in the declared file set.
